title: Retire the bespoke harness, retain the valuable parts
summary: Delete the hand-rolled timing/report/judge/dataset/runner modules the Phase 1b audit marked DISCARD; keep and relocate the four modules it marked KEEP.
description:
Per the Phase 1b audit table, delete `benchmarks/common/timing.py` (superseded by pytest-benchmark's own warmup/outlier-rejection/JSON export), `benchmarks/common/report.py` (superseded by github-action-benchmark), `benchmarks/common/llm_judge.py` (the documented root cause of BENCH-1's confounded Run A — non-deterministic verdicts), `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/dataset.py` (synthetic, template-generated, explicitly non-comparable to published figures per its own report text), `benchmarks/latency_cost/run.py` (no warmup, no statistical treatment), and `scripts/run_benchmarks.py` (superseded by `pytest -m benchmark` / `locust -f`). Retain and relocate `benchmarks/common/embedding_providers.py`, `benchmarks/common/scope_gen.py`, `benchmarks/common/cost_tracking.py`, `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/consolidator.py`, and `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/reconciler.py` into the new structure BM-3 will assemble. Prune `tests/test_benchmarks_unit.py` down to only the tests covering the retained modules. Update `Makefile` targets accordingly.

**Do not start this story until TRU-5 (EPIC-11) and BRUN-1, BRUN-2, BRUN-3 (EPIC-12) are Done or explicitly marked abandoned** — check their status on the board first. All four depend on exactly the modules this story deletes. Acceptance: `pytest` green including the 85% coverage gate; no dangling imports; the retained modules have unchanged public behavior, verified by the surviving unit tests. Depends on BM-1.

comments.text: 6 files deleted (timing.py, report.py, llm_judge.py, dataset.py, latency_cost/run.py, scripts/run_benchmarks.py). 5 modules retained. tests/test_benchmarks_unit.py pruned to 10 tests covering retained modules. Makefile updated to use pytest -m benchmark_pr. Test suite: 1009 passed, 89.78% coverage.
